newsitem.title: UK: UK soccer fan wins damages for brother's death.
newsitem.headline: UK soccer fan wins damages for brother's death.

text.p: A Liverpool soccer fan on Wednesday won 201,729 pounds ($334,000) in damages from the police for the stress caused by his half-brother's death in the Hillsborough stadium disaster of 1989.
Teenager Ian Glover was one of 96 Liverpool supporters killed in a crush at a cup semi-final game against Nottingham Forest at the stadium in Sheffield, northern England.

John McCarthy, 35, had given Glover, his half-brother, the ticket for the game. He had a seat in a different part of the ground, and could only look on as the 96 were crushed to death in an overcrowded area of terracing, prevented by a fence from escaping on to the pitch.

"The events of that day are imprinted not only indelibly in the minds of the citizens of Liverpool but also of the nation. It was a horrendous event," Justice Michael Sachs said, giving the High Court verdict.
He awarded damages against the chief constable of the South Yorkshire force, responsible for policing the match, for the post-traumatic stress disorder suffered by McCarthy.

The tragedy was the subject of a controversial television drama, screened on December 5, which revived calls for a new public inquiry into police conduct at Hillsborough and greater compensation for relatives of the dead.
